note: For each domain: the eight steps of the workflow and the performing and ownership conditions for the eight judgment axes. Items, the results report and experience input all read this one file. `verify_targets` and `artifacts` are what the results report's action steps draw on, so they must be concrete here to avoid vague wording

workflow.name: How the problem arrives
workflow.detail: A topic to look into arrives as an assignment or a request

workflow.name: Inputs received
workflow.detail: Available databases and library holdings, deadline, existing earlier research

workflow.name: What gets decided first
workflow.detail: The search words and range to look at, and the line for materials not to use

workflow.name: Methods used
workflow.detail: Building search words, making lists, checking originals, organizing and quoting

workflow.name: Tools used
workflow.detail: Academic databases, library catalogs, reference management tools, citation styles

workflow.name: Deliverables produced
workflow.detail: Material lists, summary cards, a manuscript with matching citation format, a record of the search paths

workflow.name: What it is compared against
workflow.detail: Originals, other editions, citations in earlier research, primary and secondary sources

workflow.name: When it goes wrong
workflow.detail: If nothing comes up, separate whether the search words are the problem or the material does not exist

J1.l2: Wrote down separately the range to search this time and the range not to search
J1.l3: The range I set became the research scope of that assignment

J2.l2: Turned what to find out into search words, years and categories
J2.l3: The search conditions I wrote became the standard conditions for that place

J3.l2: Chose myself the materials to use and the materials to filter out
J3.l3: The list I chose became the bibliography as it was

J4.l2: Chose a database or organizing tool and adjusted it for use
J4.l3: Another person used the organizing method I set up as it was

J5.l2: Kept a material list and summaries
J5.l3: Another person read the list I left and continued the search

J6.l2: Checked quoted content against the original or other editions
J6.l3: Changed the material chosen for use based on the check

J7.l2: Narrowed the reason for no results down to the search words or whether the material exists
J7.l3: Changed the search method and confirmed that fewer materials were missed

J8.l2: Materials I organized were used in another person's writing
J8.l3: My list became the bibliography of a project report or a paper

org_outcomes.OC1: Material research submitted to a planning meeting
org_outcomes.OC2: Supporting materials requested by a client
org_outcomes.OC4: Reference literature for a project report
org_outcomes.OC5: Summary of earlier research for a paper
org_outcomes.OC6: Checking precedents that become the basis for a judgment
org_outcomes.OC7: Background materials for writing done alone

domains.name: Text Analysis and Interpretation

workflow.name: How the problem arrives
workflow.detail: A text or work to read arrives as an assignment

workflow.name: Inputs received
workflow.detail: The original and its editions, earlier interpretations, available theoretical frameworks, deadline

workflow.name: What gets decided first
workflow.detail: Which framework to read with, and the passages to use as evidence

workflow.name: Methods used
workflow.detail: Reading through, picking passages, reading by a framework, comparing with other interpretations

workflow.name: Tools used
workflow.detail: Originals and annotated editions, citation tools, reading notes, a list of earlier interpretations

workflow.name: Deliverables produced
workflow.detail: An analysis, a list of passages used as evidence, one page on the limits of the interpretation

workflow.name: What it is compared against
workflow.detail: Other passages of the original, earlier interpretations, other writings by the same author, materials from the same period

workflow.name: When it goes wrong
workflow.detail: If the evidence is weak, separate whether the framework does not fit or there are not enough passages

tools: Dictionaries and collections of usage examples
artifacts: List of passages used as evidence
Notes on the limits of the interpretation
verify_targets: Other writings by the same author
Results of reading from a different point of view

J1.l2: Wrote down separately the passages to read this time and the passages not to cover
J1.l3: The passages I chose became the analysis scope of that text

J2.l2: Turned what I want to know into a question that can be checked
J2.l3: The question I wrote became the topic of that presentation

J3.l2: Chose myself the reading framework and the passages to use as evidence
J3.l3: The reading I built became the basis of that class or text

J4.l2: Chose a theoretical framework or reading method and adjusted it for use
J4.l3: Another person used the reading method I used as it was

J5.l2: Kept an analysis text and a list of evidence passages
J5.l3: Another person quoted the analysis I left

J6.l2: Compared my reading with earlier interpretations or other passages
J6.l3: Changed the interpretation based on the comparison

J7.l2: Narrowed the reason for weak evidence down to the framework or the passages
J7.l3: Changed the framework and confirmed that a passage I could not explain was explained

J8.l2: My interpretation was used in discussion in a class or presentation
J8.l3: My analysis was quoted in a paper or a critique

org_outcomes.OC1: The basis of commentary and recommendation writing
org_outcomes.OC2: An analysis report requested by a client
org_outcomes.OC4: Commentary text for an exhibition or a project
org_outcomes.OC5: The analysis chapter of a paper
org_outcomes.OC6: The basis for the correct answer of a test item

domains.name: Language Structure Analysis

workflow.name: How the problem arrives
workflow.detail: A language phenomenon to explain arrives as an assignment or a question

workflow.name: Inputs received
workflow.detail: Collected example sentences, descriptions in dictionaries and grammar books, available analysis frameworks, native speaker intuition

workflow.name: What gets decided first
workflow.detail: Which units to divide into, and how far to look at counterexamples

workflow.name: Methods used
workflow.detail: Collecting example sentences, dividing units, writing rules, checking counterexamples

workflow.name: Tools used
workflow.detail: Dictionaries and collections of usage examples, grammar books, example cards, writing guidelines, transcription symbols

workflow.name: Deliverables produced
workflow.detail: Analysis descriptions, lists of examples and counterexamples, rule summaries, term definitions

workflow.name: What it is compared against
workflow.detail: Descriptions in dictionaries and grammar books, examples from other dialects or periods, judgments of native speakers

workflow.name: When it goes wrong
workflow.detail: If something cannot be explained, separate whether the units are wrong or there are not enough examples

tools: Dictionaries and collections of usage examples
artifacts: List of examples and of examples that break the rules
verify_targets: Explanations in dictionaries and grammar books
Judgment of people who speak that language as their native language
Example sentences that break the rules

J1.l2: Wrote down separately the phenomena to explain this time and the phenomena to leave for later
J1.l3: The range I set became the subject of that description

J2.l2: Turned what to explain into conditions that can be checked
J2.l3: The conditions I wrote became the range where that rule applies

J3.l2: Decided myself the units to divide into and the range of counterexamples to look at
J3.l3: The units I set became the way of description in that place

J4.l2: Chose an analysis framework or a transcription method and adjusted it for use
J4.l3: Another person used the transcription method I set up as it was

J5.l2: Kept an analysis description and a list of examples
J5.l3: Another person used the rule summary I left

J6.l2: Checked my description against the explanation in a dictionary or a grammar book
J6.l3: Changed the units or rules based on the check

J7.l2: Narrowed the reason something could not be explained down to the units or the examples
J7.l3: Changed the units and confirmed that there were fewer counterexamples

J8.l2: My description went into a textbook or a dictionary as an explanation
J8.l3: My rule summary became the basis of another person's analysis

org_outcomes.OC4: The basis of public language guidelines
org_outcomes.OC5: The description chapter of a paper
org_outcomes.OC6: Rules that become the basis for the correct answer of a test item
org_outcomes.OC7: Writing standards for texts written alone

review_note: In language and literature majors, roles that read texts, roles that make texts and roles that teach sit in one file. What keeps them apart is `required_axes`: translation and editing depend on failure and correction, because half of that work is receiving comments and fixing. Education, creative writing and content depend on outputs: if nothing remains, you cannot say you taught or wrote. Literature research, interpretation, assessment, area studies and research design depend on comparison and verification. So even if six axes are confirmed, the evidence does not hold when a required axis of that domain is empty
